summary: reed never persists a terminal box; every operation re-derives it fresh. On CLI attach, internal/reedcli/attach.go reads the operator's own terminal via golang.org/x/term and passes cols/rows into Engine.AttachArgv, which pins status/window-size options, reads their EFFECTIVE values back via display-message to confirm the pin actually took (this readback-vs-intent check is the closest thing to a geometry reconciliation point -- a mismatch suppresses the chained select-layout and falls back to a bare attach), then plans a layout against the client's told box and chains select-layout onto the attach-session argv so it lands only after tmux has already resized the window to the client. On every other op (Up, Resume, add/remove strand), reedengine/spawn.go's reconcileApplyPersistLocked calls applyLayoutLocked, which queries tmux's live window size directly (windowsize.go's liveBoxLocked, falling back to config on error) and reapplies select-layout against it -- this is what re-establishes correct geometry on Resume/reattach after a resize while detached. tmux itself silently rescales a layout string proportionally if its embedded dimensions ever disagree with the live window, which is precisely why nothing is cached: every planning call re-queries live geometry rather than trusting a stale value.
open_questions: The task's wording ('SIGWINCH-style live resize while already attached') is not something reed itself handles -- once attached, tmux's own client owns terminal resize; reed's geometry logic only runs at attach-time and at each engine op (Up/Resume/Add/Remove), not on a continuous resize signal. Treated 're-attaching' and 'each engine op recomputing against the live window' as the relevant reconciliation surface, since that's the only place this codebase implements geometry logic.
